questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I study French language and culture, it was important for me to go to a country/city that share the French language and culture. I picked Paris as I have stayed in a small French city beforehand and therefore wanted the "capital city" experience. It was also important for me to go to one of the universities that are a part of the Erasmus-exhange with UCPH, as I did not want to bother with more bureaucratic papers than necessary, hence why I chose Sorbonne Université.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. We had no idea when we would have our first introduction meeting or when the first day of school was. I had to arrive in Paris not knowing when I was starting my Exchange program. We had received an acceptance letter from Sorbonne Université with a mixture of dates from last year and this year.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had introduction meetings with general information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in the Cité Universitaire which is okay and cheap, however very far away from my university, as I had classes at Sorbonne Malesherbes. It took me 45 minutes each way with 3 different metros. However, I have not had any problems in the Cité Universitaire and I've been comfortable and safe.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can take a while with public transportation in Paris and there are often problems throughout the day that interrupts the services. If you have the opportunity to rent a place you can share with either other Erasmus students or (preferably if you want to learn French) French people, I would recommend doing that. Otherwise the Cité Universitaire is also a nice place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
In short: be patient. Expect to get all information at the last minute.
The registration process was to be honest fairly easy. But be prepared that even though you may have picked some courses from the catalog beforehand, not all of them will be available for Erasmus students. You also have to put time aside to figure out what classes you want at what time, as you create your own schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not need help, but I am sure there are coordinated people assigned to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The first 2-3 weeks are "open", which means you can attend all courses and change your courses if you'd rather have something else. I ended up changing 2 things (one concerning my time and schedule, and the other the teacher). Which was fairly easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The faculties are divided in different places. I only had courses from the French bachelor from the first semester, and they are all at the Malesherbes campus. The third year is at the City Center Sorbonne (close to Panthéon), as well as the masters. So just keep in mind what semester, what faculty and what campus your course is held at.

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only had BA-courses from the first semester of the French language bachelor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In short: it's more 'old-shool' (and not in a good way).
All courses are divided in two: one seminar style class (CM: cours magistral) and then a more intimate (up to 30ish people) class (TD: travaux dirigés). All the CM's are just a big amphitheater with a teacher speaking however she/he prefers. It can be with or without powerpoints/notes/etc. Sometimes you can ask questions, other times not. The TD's vary a lot depending on the teacher. There is a different more visible hierarchy in the French culture, and the teachers words are therefore sometimes seen as the only words acceptable. It is not very critical thinking oriented and you do not always get the chance to develop your own ideas or ways of thinking.
Exams: everything is done in hand at the table with no notes. And you will have a lot of exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
L1LFB011: Grammaire et histoire de la langue 4 ECTS
L1LF21SL: Sociolinguistique et psycholinguistique 4 ECTS
L1LM11FR: Approches des genres littéraires 8 ECTS
L1LI41LM: Écrire et penser la fiction – I 4 ECTS
L1LM19CG: Histoire de la culture occidentale pour LM 5 ECTS
L1LI18FR: Histoire du cinéma 6 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Grammaire et histoire de la langue: with Helène Biu as the TD teacher. She is absolutely wonderful and nice and just overall a good teacher.
Sociolinguistique et psycholinguistique: this is a sort of 'easy' course, however the exams are multiple choice primarily concerning what, when and who questions. So you have to do a lot of memory by heart for this one.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's an expensive city, so you will probably go over your budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Just living and bying food. When you go on Exchange you also want to have fun, and going out (eating, drinking, etc.) costs money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of different sports etc. available but I did not participate in anything like that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Check out the sports programme. They also have something called Parismus, which is young people doing stuff together (cinema, walking tours, etc.).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It's a big city, so whatever you're interested in. Plan your weekends and try new stuff as much as possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, but I am very familiar with the French culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had classes with young people (17-18ish), and I am myself 24, so I became friends with other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How annoying French people are during class. The students speak/whisper (depends) all the time during all classes. So yeah, if you get easily distracted, good luck. Sometimes you can figure out where to sit and how to avoid the worst of it, but other times you just have to try and ignore it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The history of the language and the nation. The food and the after work apéro. The art, music, etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient. Begin setting money aside now and spend wisely when you're there. Go out and see and try new stuff whenever possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have attendance at most of the classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The teachers and the exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
